message.content:
I now understand the bug completely. The fix commit `f126e71e3` explains:

> An invalid code point can trigger a call to forceEOF in JSLexer::error and set the curCharPtr_ pointer to the end of the buffer, and JSLexer::consumeBracedCodePoint continues to use curCharPtr_ past the end of the buffer.
> JSLexer::error calls forceEOF and returns false when the error limit is reached.

So the bug is: when the error limit is reached, `JSLexer::error` calls `forceEOF` which sets `curCharPtr_` to `bufferEnd_` (or past it), and returns false. But `consumeBracedCodePoint` ignores the return value of `error()` and continues the loop, reading past the end of the buffer.

The test case is: `'\u{12XXXXXXXXXXX'` (a string literal with a non-terminated braced code point with many invalid characters to hit the error limit).

Let me understand the exact trigger. The test uses `sm.setErrorLimit(1)` to reach the error limit faster. But in the fuzzer, the error limit is the default. Let me check what the default error limit is.

Let me look at the `error` function and `forceEOF`.
